newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran dismisses nuclear technology fears.
newsitem.headline: Iran dismisses nuclear technology fears.

text.p: Iran said on Thursday its armed forces would respond decisively to any hostile move against the Islamic republic and dismissed Israeli disquiet over reported Russian technology sales.
The state news agency IRNA, quoting an Iranian military official, said Iran did not need to use non-conventional (nuclear) weapons and procured its needs from domestic resources.

The Los Angeles Times said last month that U.S. intelligence reports indicated Russia had given Israel's arch-enemy Iran technology for the Russian SS-4 missile, which has a range almost three times greater than that of any missile now in Tehran's arsenal. Moscow denied the report.
Moscow's ties with Tehran are an irritant in Israel's relations with Russia, which has signed an $800 million deal to complete an Iranian nuclear reactor in the southern port of Bushehr.
The West fears that Tehran might use the technology to develop nuclear weapons.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ending a 48-hour visit to Moscow on Wednesday, said he raised with Russian leaders the question of ballistic missile and nuclear technology flowing to Iran.

"I was assured by President Yeltsin that the nuclear cooperation was on a very rudimentary level and that the ballistic missile development, he said, was not taking place and will not take place," Netanyahu told a news conference.
"Since this is an ongoing concern of ours, we agreed to have further conversations on this point to clarify our concerns and to insure indeed that this threat does not materialise."
IRNA said the Iranian military official, whom it did not name, described Iran's conventional military cooperation with other countries as a routine practice at international level.
He also said Iran had repeatedly expressed its interest in promoting its defensive cooperation in the Gulf and with neighbouring countries and had taken steps in this direction.

The official dismissed Israeli remarks on Iran's non-conventional military purchases as allegations raised to shift elsewhere the crisis over controversial plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
